data.name: Kean
data.gender_notes: Kean is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'keanos', meaning 'of Crete' or 'vigorous, strong'. In Greek mythology, Kean was a son of Apollo and a Lycian princess, or a legendary Cretan king. In Christianity, Saint Kean of Crete is a revered martyr. The name Kean carries the meaning “Strong, vigorous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kean usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, vigorous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and endurance in the face of challenges and adversity.
data.etymology: Kean belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, vigorous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kean total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kean" has ancient Greek origins and was once associated with the powerful and respected civilization of Crete. In modern usage, it carries a sense of strength, robustness, and connection to the past.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kean holds special significance for Christians as it is the name of Saint Kean of Crete, a revered martyr who is said to have suffered extreme persecution during the Roman Empire and ultimately offered his life to uphold his faith. His legacy inspires courage, resilience, and unwavering commitment to one's beliefs in the face of adversity.
